explanation:
[EFFECT] Weather acts as a step function across four categories. Clear skies (category 1) give a small positive boost (~+0.045); mist/cloud (2) is nearly neutral (~0); light rain or snow (3) substantially suppresses demand (~–0.35); and heavy rain (4) also suppresses demand (~–0.25) — slightly less than category 3 in this model.
[IMPORTANCE] Sixth in importance (0.061); meaningful but smaller in magnitude than temperature or year.
[RECOMMENDATION] Hour of day and temperature are by far the two strongest drivers of predicted demand, so operational planning — such as bike redistribution and staffing — should be tightly organised around the two daily rush-hour peaks (around 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m.) and scaled up noticeably in mild to warm weather while scaling back during cold spells or the early hours of the morning.
